Hi all — adding the technical implementation detail requested. Below is a condensed plan we typically deliver for enterprise migrations; I've called out owners and acceptance gates.

Phased timeline (recommended)
- Week 0 (Prep, 1 week): Account provisioning, IAM mapping, KMS setup (customer or Redwood-managed), network validation (VPC peering + firewall rules), HubSpot deal kickoff.
- Week 1-2 (Pilot, 2 weeks): Connect dev/test tenant, validate auth tokens, schema mapping for embedding and metadata fields, integration tests for inferencing endpoints, smoke load (~10 qps). Acceptance: <1% request error, p50 latency within target.
- Week 3-5 (Canary, 3 weeks): Traffic ramp schedule: Day 0-3: 1% traffic; Day 4-10: 5%; Day 11-21: 20-30% depending on results. Evaluation windows after each ramp: 24–72h. Key metrics: error rate, p95/p99 latency, token cost variance, quality regressions on evaluation prompts. Rollback criteria: sustained error rate >1.5% over 3 hours OR p95 latency increase >2x baseline OR evaluation set regression >4%.
- Week 6-8 (Staged broad rollout, 2–3 weeks): 50% -> 100% ramp by segment, final validation and post-cutover monitoring for 7 days.

Integration steps (high level)
- Auth: OAuth2 token exchange + role bindings; option for mTLS for private deployments.
- API endpoints: /v1/generate, /v1/chat, /v1/embeddings. Payload schema v2 — we provide JSON schema and example clients.
- Data flows: Inference payloads are ephemeral; customer controls persistence. For embeddings, we recommend ID mapping in client-managed DB. No persistent PII stored by Redwood unless explicitly configured.
- DB migrations: None required on Redwood side; customer DB changes limited to storing model ids and trace ids for audit linking.

Operational runbook excerpts
- Pre-cutover checklist: validate TLS certs, KMS key ops, sample token issuance, run smoke tests, confirm log shipping to customer SIEM.
- Canary gate check: run automated evaluation suite (20 prompt families), confirm health metrics, manual ops signoff if an automated gate fails.
- Rollback: switch traffic routing at the gateway (within 1 minute), revert model pin, invalidate caching layer for prefix mismatches, and notify stakeholders.

SLOs & fallbacks
- Typical latency SLOs we target per model class (lower-latency tiers available in Dedicated): p95 < 350ms for short prompts (<=256 tokens) under target QPS.
- Fallbacks: policy-based fallback to smaller/cheaper model variant or queueing with informative retries for non-critical workloads.

Attachments I'll add: the canary runbook excerpt and a CSV mapping of endpoints to contract line items.

-Karthik

Daniel —

Appreciate the questions. Short answers:

1) Logs & APM: Yes — we support log forwarding to customer SIEMs including Splunk via secure syslog/HTTPS endpoints. Field-level redaction can be configured on the shipping agent; we'll list necessary redaction rules in the final evidence bundle.
2) Automated rollback: supported. We provide configurable automated safety gates that can trigger rollback when defined metrics cross thresholds. We generally recommend automated rollback for error-rate/latency triggers and manual review for quality-evaluation regressions, but we can enable an automated rollback on eval regression if Novacore wants (we recommend a short manual hold window 15–30 minutes to confirm false positives).

Next steps: we've attached the final artifacts for the RFP response (matrix + runbook + checklist mapping). Proposed pilot start: 2026-05-18. I'll upload the documents to the HubSpot record and send the DocuSign envelope for the pilot SOW.

Thanks and speak soon,
Marcus Lin
